utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will the usher please show Exhibit D66/2. It is a photograph. Could it be, please, shown to the witness to see if he can identify it, D66/2. [In English] Could I ask Mr. Usher to put it on the ELMO, please, the colour one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you recognise the house that we were talking about, that is, Marijan Skopljak's house, and the restaurant Konaba?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the restaurant Konaba, and we met in this auxiliary building [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that that was a kind of operative headquarters of the staff of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that in two smallish rooms which had not been furnished properly or even finished properly, there was no plaster or anything but there was a table and a couple of chairs, and that was, among all the things, where we met and also discussed the evacuation of my family from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, you already said that the principal objective the HVO pursued in the municipality of Vitez and beyond it in Central Bosnia was to structure itself, to organise itself, so as to better resist the advancing forces of the army of Bosnian Serbs and the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, you mentioned that you participated and that there were certain military operations organised with a view to moving out the JNA units from the barracks in adjacent places and takeover of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Organised with me as the head of the operation, that is, after my arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this action was not participated only by the HVO members but also members of the Territorial Defence, that is, Bosniaks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It is, insofar as they were able to take part or, rather, insofar as I could trust the units that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of these actions was the taking over of the barracks at Slimena. If I am correct, you took part in that action personally; rather, you commanded that action.

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if my client, Mr. Cerkez, under the orders of Mr. Marijan Skopljak, was also to take part in that action?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: He was to take part in that action, and he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, General, you managed to get two anti-aircraft cannons for that action from the municipal staff of the TO?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: A three-barrel cannon of 20 millimetres and Bofors, and they were manned by mixed crews of the TO and the HVO; not only those cannons. But I found, when I arrived and then participated in equipping that battery, because we wanted it to serve as an example to all the other units, it was a mixed crew made up of Muslims and Croats, but the majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But this was an action which was jointly organised. It was no secret action that would have been conducted by only and exclusively by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was secret insofar as when you organise something, it does require certain secrecy, but not an action conducted by the HVO. There had been, before that, negotiations with Cengic, with Hamdija Cengic in Vitez, and I think that General Merdan and Dugalic also took part in it as regards the activity and distribution of the weaponry in that depot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, General, if I was somewhat confused. When I said "secret," I meant secret in the sense that it was hidden from the Muslims or, rather, the TO. It was you did not conceal that action from them. But you've already answered my question.

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You also said that Mr. Cerkez took part in that operation. Was his task to bring the volunteers from Vitez at a certain time to a certain place where the action was to start?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, that was his task. But he wasn't a surety, but he was a kind of a man I could trust, really, so he made me feel more secure, because I negotiated with the chief of that depot under sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His name was Kostic?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Kostic, to try to resolve it in a manner worthy of military and saying that they should be allowed to leave with their personal weapons in a manner that military should do; that is, not to surrender but simply to pull out and go to their people, that is, in the barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But those negotiations failed?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I saw it in his eyes, that nothing would come out of these negotiations, and at night he just blew up the depot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the HVO and TO came by a certain quantity of weaponry. Could you tell us, how was it distributed?

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: These weapons, I mean, from Slimena were not distributed, but the crowd went through the security guards that we had positioned to avoid any casualties. But the crowd simply passed upon that field and began to grab it, to grab the materiel which was there scattered over all the meadows and fields and whatnot. And I know that General Merdan and Dugalic arrived with several trucks, and I also know that from the municipal staffs of the HVO, groups came in vehicles and took materiel away. So it was not distributed. It was snatched, grabbed, and plundered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I used the wrong term. It was a misnomer. I should have said -- I should have asked whether the TO army, that is, the Bosnian side, got any of the weapons that had been kept in the depot.

utterances.speaker: FILIP FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the barrels and personal weapons are concerned, they took much more -- a much larger share than the HVO. And that is what I claim, what I affirm, because there were wounded and I believe there were even some fatality, and they show that they were all Muslims. That day, I did not have a single Croat casualty, but that night there was fighting, and two HVO members were killed and eight of them sustained severe injuries. When the commander blew up those facilities, then that and all the rubble and materiel simply buried the men who were besieging the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like to move to another topic, so perhaps this would be a convenient time to break for today. I mean you said that we would be working until 4.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Half past 9.00, please, tomorrow morning. Would you be back, Major General Filipovic, then, for half past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
